text:
Alex Kim: quick ask — where's the canonical place to grab a TTFT breakdown (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec for a single request-id? I need slices for an RCA. Which dashboards/panels + traces do you all use?

Maria Gomez: there are a couple. For quick eyeballing: Grafana "Latency: per-route pxx + token-rate" dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.net/d/latency/per-route-latency). Panel names: "TTFT p50/p95/p99 (route)" and "Tokens/sec (route)".

Jeff R.: if you want a PromQL starting point for a single request slice, use the request_id label and these queries: 
```
# TTFT p95 for request_id X (histogram_quantile over summary metric)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{request_id="REQ123"}[1m])) by (le))

# token rate per second for request_id X
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total{request_id="REQ123"}[1m])) by (request_id)
```
Swap the window for longer windows if you need smoother curves.

Lina Chen: jaeger link for the same trace: https://jaeger.redwood.net/trace/REQ123 — filters work well if you open the request span and expand child spans to see decoding/kv/cache time. Also check the "prefix-cache-hit" spans — those usually explain p95 tail.

Alex Kim: nice — is the tokens/sec metric definitely tokens_emitted_total? I thought we also had tokens_per_request somewhere. Want to be sure I'm pulling the right one for cost vs latency correlation.

Maria Gomez: tokens_emitted_total is cumulative; tokens_per_request is a derived gauge we emit post-request (useful for per-request cost). For token-rate over time use tokens_emitted_total with rate(), for per-request correlation join with tokens_per_request by request_id.

Jeff R.: FYI the TTFT panels are set up to use the service-level rollup by default. If you need the raw pod-level traces, switch the dashboard variable "instance" to "all". Also: if you're hunting p99, increase the histogram bucket resolution in query to 5m windows sometimes helps.

obs-bot: Alert: ttft-p99-high (route=/generate) triggered at 2026-05-04T11:02:12Z — p99 = 1.9s > threshold 1.5s. Incident doc: https://redwood-internal/ops/incidents/462

Lina Chen: regarding alerts — for this specific route we were discussing moving p99 threshold to 2.0s during peak ramp and relying on tokens/sec anomaly to catch regressions. If you want, I can open a small PR to tune the alert to `p99 > 2s for 5m` with a suppress window for daily batch jobs. Need one reviewer.

Alex Kim: please do, Lina. Tag me and Maria as reviewers. I'll attach the trace and the PromQL I ran.

Maria Gomez: quick snippet to grab a trace id from logs if you only have request-id: 
```
# get trace id from service logs (k8s)
kubectl logs deploy/inference-service -n prod --since=10m | rg "REQ123" | rg -o "trace_id=[a-f0-9]+" | head -n1
```

Jeff R.: one more tip — when you export the p95/p99 timeseries panel you can use the panel's CSV export and then join with the tokens-per-request CSV by request_id for a simple correlation table. Saves fiddling with complex promQL joins.

Alex Kim: perfect, thanks everyone. I'll run the queries, attach the CSVs and paste the trace link in the RCA thread later today. :thumbsup:

Lina Chen: ping me if you want the alert PR drafted. I'll also drop a quick runbook note on where to look for prefix-cache spans.

Alex Kim: will do.
